decisions.statement: A reading answers that a subagent is working, has returned, or was not read.
Not knowing is answered as its own reading rather than as a subagent returned.
A subagent the transcript names as running reads as working.
A transcript recording a result for the subagent reads as returned.
A transcript read naming the subagent nowhere reads as unread.
A subagent a transcript names nowhere may be working rather than returned.
A seat stating no transcript reads as unread.
A transcript that will not open reads as unread.
A page whose own agent id will not be read reads as unread.
A reading that ends in an error reads as unread.
The seat whose transcript is read is named by the agent id the page states.
A subagent the transcript names below another subagent is named as one at the top is.
A result recorded below another subagent is read as one at the top is.
That holds though whatever recorded the result has itself returned.
The id a subagent runs under is taken from the page where a caller names none.
A reading says which of its steps settled the answer.
A page stating no agent id and a seat stating no transcript are told apart by that reason.
A reading that ends in an error carries what was thrown into that reason.
A reading is asked for by the ids a process carries as well as by a page.
Nothing here writes that reason anywhere.
Nothing here takes a page away, writes one, or lands anything.

definition: what a seat's transcript says of whether a subagent is still running
